_description: Scheduled jobs in a container: Alpine + BusyBox crond in the foreground, PHP CLI available, crontabs and scripts bind-mounted from the host.
_comment: A RECIPE: `uxc deploy cron` builds a small Alpine image with crond + PHP CLI, creates /srv/cron/{crontabs,scripts,state}, seeds an example crontab and a health-check script, and registers the container. This is for a job that must run INSIDE a container next to your application (a CMS scheduler, a cache purge). uxcd's own per-container schedules restart/stop/start whole containers instead - see docs/configuration.md; the two do not overlap.

build._comment_dockerfile: PHP CLI + the extension set a CMS scheduler usually wants, plus flock and tzdata. Drop the php85-* packages if your jobs are shell only. Alpine's php85-* packages install in seconds - unlike compiling extensions, which is why this container builds fast even on a router.
dockerfile: php85 php85-phar php85-mbstring php85-iconv php85-openssl php85-curl \
php85-zip php85-dom php85-simplexml php85-xml php85-xmlreader php85-xmlwriter \
php85-gd php85-intl php85-exif php85-fileinfo php85-session php85-tokenizer \

_comment_seed: An example job and the health-check script. Both are written only when absent. The crontab file name IS the user the jobs run as - 'root' here, with the job itself dropping to uid 82 via su.

/srv/cron/crontabs/root: # Crontab written by `uxc deploy cron`. EDIT ME.
# BusyBox crond: min hour day month weekday command
# The example below runs every minute and only touches the state file the
# health check looks at, so a fresh container is healthy out of the box.
# Replace it with your real job; keep (or update) the touch, or the health
# check will report unhealthy after ten minutes.
# A CMS scheduler as uid 82, one at a time, capped at 5 minutes:

content: # Example job written by `uxc deploy cron`. Replace with your own.
# Records a successful run for the health check.
# Health check written by `uxc deploy cron`.
# Unhealthy when crond is not running, or when no job has recorded a
# successful run in the last 10 minutes - a crond that is up but whose
# jobs all fail is not a healthy scheduler.
pgrep crond >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'crond is not running'; exit 1; }
[ -f /state/last-run ] || { echo 'no job has run yet'; exit 1; }
[ "$age" -le 600 ] || { echo "last successful run was ${age}s ago"; exit 1; }

_registry._comment_health: start_period covers the first minute, before any job has had a chance to run.
_registry.notes: Deployed from the 'cron' recipe. Crontabs: /srv/cron/crontabs (the FILE NAME is the user the jobs run as); scripts: /srv/cron/scripts (must be executable); run state: /srv/cron/state. The health check needs a job to touch /state/last-run at least every 10 minutes. Set TZ in the registry env if UTC is wrong for your jobs. Job output goes to the container log: `uxc log cron`. Test a job by hand with `uxe cron /opt/jobs/<name>`.
